title: Determine the sharp connectivity threshold for homogeneous Kuramoto synchronization
domain: Dynamics on networks and collective behavior
statement: For finite simple undirected graphs with identical natural frequencies and unit positive edge coupling, let mu_c be the infimum of thresholds guaranteeing convergence to the all-in-phase state from almost every initial phase configuration whenever minimum degree/(n-1) exceeds the threshold. Determine whether mu_c = 3/4. This concerns nonlinear almost-everywhere global synchronization, not merely the absence of positive eigenvalues at selected equilibria.
source_locator: Kassabov et al., abstract and Sections I, VI; McRae (2026 v2), Section 3.4.3; Lepsveridze and Zhang (2026), Theorem 1, footnote 1 and Remark 1; O'Keeffe (2026), Section I, footnotes 1–2 and Theorem 1
status_basis: The dynamical 3/4 conjecture remains source-reported open. Later papers distinguish it from a local-minimum conjecture and report new bounds; see the dated literature check. These preprint claims have not received independent review here.

revision_history.change: Added later sources and clarified their distinct threshold definitions; preserved the original dynamical statement and pending human review.

plain_summary: How dense must a network be to make identical phase oscillators synchronize from almost all starting phases? The historical target is whether three quarters is sharp for this dynamical guarantee. A weaker condition, absence of nonsynchronous local minima, must be assessed separately.
assumptions: A finite simple undirected graph with n≥2, adjacency A_ij∈{0,1}, no loops, and minimum-degree density delta(G)/(n−1).
Identical natural frequencies are removed by a rotating frame; theta_dot_i=sum_j A_ij sin(theta_j−theta_i). Coupling is positive and unweighted.
Phases lie on a torus. Uniform phase rotation is a symmetry; stability statements must be interpreted after quotienting that direction.
Global synchronization means convergence to equal phases from almost every initial phase, with respect to torus Lebesgue measure.
scope: The literature target ranges over all finite graphs. A curator-proposed first milestone explores connected circulants with 8≤n≤32 and twisted equilibria theta_j=2pi qj/n, 1≤q<n. At most 1,000 declared (graph,q) pairs are considered. This family and cap are not asserted novel or sufficient to settle the threshold.
target: Develop a proof of sharpness or a stronger universal synchronization theorem. A bounded first deliverable is a fully checkable stable nonsynchronized equilibrium certificate or a precisely delimited list of inconclusive or unstable cases.
success_criteria: Record the graph, connectivity, degree, phase pattern and exact equilibrium equations.

To certify a useful local obstruction, prove the Jacobian is strictly negative definite on the complement of the uniform-rotation vector. Explain why this gives an open basin and defeats almost-everywhere synchronization.
If any additional eigenvalue is zero, report nonlinear stability as unresolved unless a separate nonlinear argument is supplied.
Report the achieved degree density exactly and compare it with prior constructions. A finite example or failed search does not establish mu_c=3/4.
known_results: Kassabov, Strogatz and Townsend prove the sufficient 3/4 density threshold.
McRae's August 2026 Section 3.4.3 records the historical sharpness conjecture; later sources below distinguish its formulations.

Townsend, Stillman and Strogatz provide explicit circulant constructions and spectra. Examples approaching 3/4 with marginal second-order conditions are not automatically stable nonlinear obstructions.

Lepsveridze and Zhang (SRC-FORMAL-619) report a strict upper bound below 3/4 for the local-minimum threshold, refuting that version of the conjecture. Their normalization is (delta+1)/n; Remark 1 leaves the dynamical extension unfinished.

O'Keeffe (SRC-FORMAL-620) reports a lower bound mu_0=(4+2q*)/(7+q*)=0.6929077063... for both thresholds. Here q* is the unique root in (0,1) of 9q^8+72q^7+288q^6+448q^5+470q^4+88q^3−208q^2−128q−15. Section I retains 3/4 as the dynamical upper bound.
prerequisites: Kuramoto gradient dynamics, equilibria and stability modulo a continuous symmetry.
Circulant matrices, Fourier diagonalization and exact algebraic or certified interval arithmetic.
The difference between an equilibrium, a local minimum, a second-order critical point and almost-everywhere convergence.
significance: A sharp threshold would connect graph density with a global nonlinear property. Small certified constructions can guide a structural argument, but duplicating a known family does not improve the bound.

relations.explanation: The cycle-spectrum task checks phase conventions and treatment of zero eigenvalues before extending to general circulants.
Random cubic synchronization is a different asymptotic question; it does not follow from a high minimum-degree criterion.

requirements.experiment: None for the homogeneous graph model. Testing real oscillator networks requires measured frequencies, coupling, noise and model adequacy.
requirements.data: Explicit adjacency matrices and exact phase parameters; no observed time series is required.
requirements.compute: Suggested pilot cap: 1,000 (graph,q) pairs, n≤32, one CPU-hour and 8 GiB memory, with timeouts marked unresolved. These are proposed limits, not benchmarks. Small circulant spectra support inexpensive numerical filtering, but exact sign certificates and proofs about all graph sizes may be substantially harder. SRC-FORMAL-620, Section V, describes an existence construction with more than 9×10^84 vertices; the pilot is not a direct reproduction of those graphs.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: Identical frequencies, unit positive symmetric coupling, deterministic sine interaction, finite simple graphs and almost-everywhere initial phases.

ai_assessment.rationale: AI can suggest graph families and derive spectra while exact arithmetic checks stability. Expert review must prevent a marginal linear condition from being mistaken for a nonlinear obstruction.

clarity.reason: The graph class, dynamics and degree normalization are explicit.

decomposability.reason: Graph generation, equilibrium verification and spectral certification are separate tasks.

methods.reason: The sources give explicit circulant methods and sharp sufficient criteria.

search_or_symbolic.reason: Small structured graphs admit finite search and symbolic eigenvalue calculations.

checkability.reason: Strict spectral certificates are checkable; degenerate equilibria require nonlinear analysis.

expertise.reason: Dynamical systems and extremal graph expertise are needed.

significance.reason: The threshold is a meaningful global synchronization question.

verification_difficulty.reason: Linear degeneracies and the all-graph quantifier are serious obstacles.

ai_assessment.uncertainty: The small circulant family may only recover known examples. The pilot has not been evaluated; external AI-assisted work does not establish its likely success.
ai_assessment.model_scope: No named model evaluated; assumes tool-using AI able to manipulate exact formulas, generate auditable code and explain mathematical assumptions.

methods: Symmetry-guided graph construction and twisted equilibria.
Exact Fourier spectra over cyclotomic fields, or rigorous interval enclosures with justified sign separation.
Independent rational or algebraic certificates for the reduced Jacobian.
Minimal-obstruction analysis and nonlinear normal-form arguments when strict stability fails.
obstacles: Absence of positive Jacobian eigenvalues does not establish nonlinear attraction when additional zero eigenvalues occur.
A few stable examples cannot prove sharpness without a sequence approaching the threshold.
A theorem about local minima needs careful comparison with the dynamical almost-everywhere definition.

steps: Reconstruct A from the saved edge list, verify simplicity, symmetry and connectivity, and compute delta(G)/(n−1) exactly.
Check every equilibrium residual using exact trigonometric identities; floating-point cancellation is insufficient.
Construct J_ij=A_ij cos(theta_j−theta_i) off diagonal and J_ii=−sum_(j≠i)J_ij independently from the search routine.
Verify the rotation zero mode and exact strict negativity on its orthogonal complement with a separate algebraic or certified-interval implementation.
Explain the nonlinear implication of strict reduced stability, and have a dynamics specialist audit any extra-zero case.
Compare any claimed density improvement or graph family against the cited constructions and later literature before naming it new.
validation.human_review_difficulty: Medium for a strict finite-dimensional certificate after conventions are fixed; high for marginal equilibria, graph-size limits or a universal threshold proof.
validation.statement_alignment: Retain unit symmetric coupling, identical frequencies, density divided by n−1 and almost-everywhere convergence. Stable nonuniform equilibria are sufficient obstructions; marginal critical points alone are not.

known_attempts: The 2020 circulant constructions, the 2021 density theorem and the 2026 normalized-Laplacian analysis are external records. No project search or simulation has been run.
The 2026 preprints SRC-FORMAL-619 and SRC-FORMAL-620 supply later external results. O'Keeffe reports AI-assisted research; its proofs and computations have not been reproduced here.
unresolved_checks: Establish whether a proposed finite family or density has already been classified.
Determine nonlinear behavior separately whenever the reduced Jacobian is singular.
Compare proposed improvements with SRC-FORMAL-620 and subsequent work; independently review its proof and obtain the supporting scripts before claiming a reproduction.

epistemic_layers.formal_validity: Any certificate establishes a fact only for the specified homogeneous Kuramoto equations and graph. Strict reduced stability has a mathematical local-basin interpretation.
epistemic_layers.empirical_support: Real synchronization depends on frequency mismatch, weights, noise and the adequacy of sine coupling. This formal task supplies no observational or experimental support for those assumptions.
